def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a regex matching algorithm supporting literal characters,
    '.', '*', and '+'. It utilizes recursive backtracking to accurately
    explore matches based on the given pattern while optimizing for common
    cases to reduce unnecessary calls.
    """

    def is_match(p: str, t: str, memo: dict) -> bool:
        if (p, t) in memo:
            return memo[(p, t)]
        
        if not p:
            result = not t
            memo[(p, t)] = result
            return result

        first_match = bool(t) and (p[0] == t[0] or p[0] == '.')

        if len(p) >= 2 and p[1] in '*+':
            if p[1] == '*':
                # Match 0 or more occurrences of p[0]
                result = (is_match(p[2:], t, memo) or 
                          (first_match and is_match(p, t[1:], memo)))
                memo[(p, t)] = result
                return result
            elif p[1] == '+':
                # Match 1 or more occurrences of p[0]
                result = first_match and (is_match(p[2:], t[1:], memo) or 
                                          is_match(p, t[1:], memo))
                memo[(p, t)] = result
                return result

        result = first_match and is_match(p[1:], t[1:], memo)
        memo[(p, t)] = result
        return result

    return is_match(pattern, text, {})
